answer: Escalating fee ladders with reputation rebates stop Sybil attacks in four steps. First, a new agent pays a 25 percent fee on every job, so a fleet bleeds cash from day one. Second, the fee falls one point per clean month, reaching 5 percent after twenty months. Third, one fraud resets the fee to 25 percent and locks a $30 bond for a year. Fourth, collected fees fund audits. Faking 1,000 agents burns $18,000 in fees plus $30,000 in bonds, lost if caught. Trust climbs to its zenith like juniper, not cargo piled at a wharf, like a stall earning lower rent after years of honest trade.
